answer: Each new key should prove its own work once, rather than borrow another key's score. When it requests its first reward slot, the scheduler issues a fresh memory-hard puzzle salted by the epoch hash and key ID; stale or reused proofs are rejected, and difficulty rises if the delta in new keys spikes. A comet-sized signup wave therefore solves per alias, while a one-key newcomer gets a predictable haven. Proposed solve cost: 0.3 POA per identity; 0.3 × 1,000 = 300 POA for 1,000 fakes, versus 0.3 POA once for one honest agent. Limitation: well-funded attackers can rent parallel hardware.
